notes: KNOWN FAILING — BOTH COMMITTED RECORDINGS PREDATE #1860 AND NEITHER CAN SATISFY THIS SPEC. #1860 reverted #1800: a process exit deletes the session row again, whatever state the row was in. irrlicht is not the agent's parent, so it gets no exit status on any platform — a segfault, an OOM kill, a `kill -9` and a clean exit(0) are one observation — and #1800's guess from session shape was wrong often enough to paint an ESC interrupt and a denied tool prompt red (see #1860's reproduction). The expectation below is therefore the post-#1860 truth: process_exited fires and the row goes away, with no working→error anywhere. Both recordings were captured on daemons carrying #1800 (2026-08-25 on 0.6.0+6c65754, 2026-08-26 on 0.6.0+5c40e63), whose retain branch suppressed process_exited entirely and emitted working→error instead — so the frozen bytes assert the removed behaviour and cannot be reconciled with this spec by any daemon-side change. RE-RECORD ON A POST-#1860 DAEMON AND DROP THIS FLAG; nothing else clears it. The recordings stay on disk under the #268 deletion guard. Knowingly given up by #1860, and stated here because this cell is where it is most visible: a genuine mid-turn crash now disappears silently too. That is the accepted cost of never showing a false one.
source: #1860 (revert of #1800/#1815/#1817). Supersedes the #1803 expectation, which asserted the retained `error` row.

text: The agent process is killed mid-turn; the exit is recorded and the row is deleted. The session never goes red — the daemon cannot tell this crash from a deliberate quit (#1860).
